- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — cap forecast at 5–10% below peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of downward trend in history + negative sentiment, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) — increase initial forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.5 to -1.5 within 3 days), model misreads momentum — use sentiment average over 5 days to smooth forecast.  
- When true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with recent price mean.
